short: Massive reclamation of crown lands from the nobility, financing the absolute monarchy.
full:
Initiated in 1680 by King Charles XI, the Great Reduction was a sweeping economic and political reform that reclaimed crown lands, fiefs, and assets previously granted to the high nobility. The measure was desperately needed to restore state finances devastated by the Scanian War.

The policy fundamentally broke the political power of the aristocracy and transferred immense wealth back to the state. This financial independence allowed Charles XI to establish an absolute monarchy and fund a reorganized, standing military force without relying on the nobility or constant parliamentary taxation.
